strings.name: Shelly-Ann Fraser-Pryce
strings.role: Retired sprinter · Olympic and world champion
strings.summary: Fraser-Pryce rose from Kingston to international sprinting, known for explosive starts and lasting championship success. She won two Olympic 100m titles and five world 100m titles and returned to the top after childbirth. A positive oxycodone test brought a six-month suspension in 2010. She retired in 2025 with three Olympic golds and ten world titles and continued supporting young athletes and education.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected career milestones; results and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive results log or live ranking.
strings.influence.rationale: An Olympic and world sprint champion representing sustained excellence at the top of women's sprinting.

strings.facts.fact-2.label: Main events
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Five world 100m titles
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Won the world 100m title in 2009, 2013, 2015, 2019 and 2022.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Back-to-back Olympic 100m titles
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Won the 100m at Beijing 2008 and London 2012.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Named a Laureus Ambassador
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Joined Laureus as an ambassador, extending her post-retirement work supporting young athletes and education.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Formally announced retirement
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Confirmed retirement after her Tokyo farewell, ending a career with three Olympic golds and ten world titles.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: World relay silver in her farewell
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Finished sixth in her final world 100m final, then won 4×100m relay silver with Jamaica.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Fifth world 100m title
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Won in Oregon to become the first woman with five world 100m titles.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Tokyo Olympic relay gold
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Won 100m silver and 4×100m relay gold in Tokyo, her third Olympic gold medal.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: World titles after childbirth
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Returned after the birth of her son in 2017 to win the 100m and relay in Doha.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Three titles in Moscow
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Won the 100m, 200m and 4×100m relay at the same World Championships.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Retained the Olympic 100m title
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Retained the 100m title in London and added silver in the 200m and relay.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Suspended after an oxycodone positive
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Received a six-month ban after an oxycodone positive in Shanghai; she said she had taken it for toothache.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Olympic breakthrough in Beijing
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Became Jamaica’s first women’s Olympic 100m gold medalist in Beijing.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: World Championships debut
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Ran in the relay heats in Osaka and received silver with Jamaica.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in Kingston
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Born in Waterhouse, Kingston, and developed through school athletics in Jamaica.
